ab_a_short_pantry.description:
A desert doesn't offer much to eat, and I've learned what it does offer over four camps. Most of our meat is Pitfall Kodo. Pit Shrike's good too, if you don't mind the plucking.

You'll find both around Cartfall, west of here. The camp's larder is nearly empty, so kill some of each and I'll butcher them. I'll cook you a plate for it.
ab_a_short_pantry.accept_text: Bring the birds unplucked if you like. I've got a boy who'll do it for a biscuit.

ab_annealed.description:
Sepp put a shard of the Glasswall on my bench a month ago, from the face south of camp, and it's warm. It isn't hot. It's warm, at midnight, in a desert that goes to freezing, and I've worked glass and metal my whole life and never seen that.

Bring me more from the Glasswall Elementals, and I'll find out whether it's the stone or something in the stone. I'd like it to be the stone.
ab_annealed.accept_text: Hold one in your hand on the way back, after dark. You'll see what I mean.

ab_carry_the_book.description:
Go out by the east gate and down into the Glittervein. There's a camp at the bottom called Lastwater, and a tauren surveyor there named Ulla Stormhollow. She's been studying where the water went.

I've got the date of every collapse since the first one, three years ago, and no idea what causes them. I'm told she has a cause and no dates. Take her my log. Ask me why I'm not going myself, if you want to know.
ab_carry_the_book.accept_text: Keep it out of the wet down there. Three years of ink runs in an afternoon.

ab_drovers_in_the_sand.description:
I cooked for caravans for eleven years before this, and I'll tell you the thing about drovers. They don't stop. Weather, raiders, a broken axle, the road keeps going and so do they.

The ones out there still haven't stopped. Bring me their tags. I want to cook for a camp that's done right by them, and we haven't.

They're still on the old road at Cartfall, west of camp, and at the First Hole beyond it.
ab_drovers_in_the_sand.accept_text: Say their names out loud if you can read them on the tags, because somebody ought to.

ab_everything_points_east.description:
Sepp has brine. Hask has four shrike crops with water animals in them. Vizzi has a hundred and twenty feet of line that doesn't reach anything, twice. And there's light coming up out of the ground.

I'm a surveyor, so I don't get to say what that means. I do get to say that every single one of those points the same direction, and I want one more set of readings before I write the sentence.

Underlight is south of camp, down the east side, so start there. Bring me wet scale off the deepwater horrors, and put down the saltbone revenants on the way. They walk the ground between here and there.
ab_everything_points_east.accept_text: Write down anything you see that I didn't list. I'm trying not to lead you.

ab_feeding_from_below.description:
Go through the bestiary of this place with me. Crawlers are cave animals. Oozes are cave animals. The horrors in the Throats are aquatic. The revenants are brine.

There isn't one thing on this map that belongs in a desert except the shrikes, and the shrikes are here because everything else is here.

The entire population of this zone is a consequence of the water leaving. Bring me enough residue to say that with a number on it.

The Glasswall, south of camp, has the most of them in one place.
ab_feeding_from_below.accept_text: Put it in the stoppered jars, not a pouch. A pouch dries it, and I need it wet.

ab_four_carts.description:
Everything this camp owns has to fit on four carts, so we can pack up and leave in a day. We've done it twice. I didn't make the rule, but I was glad of it both times.

Cartfall Scavengers have been stealing our spare brass fittings, and I can't replace brass out here. They take it back to Cartfall, west of camp. Kill them and bring the brass home.
ab_four_carts.accept_text: Count it before you hand it over. I'll be counting after.

ab_fourth_peg.description:
You came in by the north gate, so you've walked nine miles of this and seen there's no road. There used to be one. It fell into a pit three years ago, with the first of the collapses.

The port at Steamwheedle pays me to find out if a new road can be built across the Abyssal Sands. I haven't got an answer yet.

Go and stand by the peg in the middle of camp, then ask me about it. We measure everything from that stake.
ab_fourth_peg.accept_text: Don't lean on it. Everybody does the first time, and then I've got to start the morning over.

ab_is_it_possible.description: I've got two years of paired readings, and I'm close to being able to say a sentence I can defend. I'd like one more set from the south, where the Saltbone Revenants walk round the Long Collapse, south-west of camp, and then I'm going to say it whether the port likes it or not. What I need is the settled residue the Hollowing Oozes leave behind, and you'll have to take it off the oozes themselves. I've never told a client no in my life, and I'd like to be sure before I start. Bring me the residue, put down the revenants, and then ask me for my answer about the road.
ab_is_it_possible.accept_text: Seal the residue the moment you take it. If it settles in your pack, it's no good to me.

ab_lit_from_below.description:
It isn't fire, because fire flickers and that doesn't. It isn't the glass either. It's the wrong colour and in the wrong place.

What it does do is get slightly brighter every season, which I've measured, and I'd like a sample of everything living within forty feet of it before I say anything about that in front of Peska.

Underlight is south of camp, down the east side, past the Glasswall. I need the glasswall elementals, the hollowing oozes, and a still-wet scale off each deepwater horror you can reach.
ab_lit_from_below.accept_text: Label which creature each sample came off. I'll be the one asked, and I'd like to have an answer.

ab_managed_not_solved.description:
Peska wants the readings. Hask wants his method. Vizzi wants a floor under every rope.

I want the camp to still be here in a month, and that's a different list, and it's mostly killing.

I'm not going to dress it up. Go and make the ground round this peg quiet for a while.

That means the sinkhole lurkers and the limestone crawlers. Kill both, and bring me the lurkers' spurs so I can show Peska the count.
ab_managed_not_solved.accept_text: Start close and work out. I'd rather the peg was safe than the far edges.

ab_never_arrived.description: You hold up the folded paper. It's a cargo manifest with the wax seal still whole, which means nobody ever got to read it at the other end. The cart it belonged to went into a pit, and the paper came up out of the sand without it. The edges are scorched by the sun, but the writing inside should be fine. The quartermaster at Fourth Peg, in the north-east corner of the Abyssal Sands, keeps the camp's freight records and might want it.
ab_never_arrived.accept_text: You slip the waybill inside your coat, seal still unbroken.

ab_nine_have_floors.description:
Somebody has to go down them. It isn't far, just far enough to see whether there's a floor and whether the floor is going anywhere.

Nine of the eleven have floors, and two don't. I'd like a second pair of hands on the line, and I'd like them attached to somebody who can fight, because the floors aren't empty.

What's on those floors is limestone crawlers. Clear them before the line goes down.
ab_nine_have_floors.accept_text: Wear gloves on the line. It burns through bare hands faster than you'd believe.

ab_nothing_is_hot_enough.description:
I've got to write up the Glasswall and I've put it off for seven months. I don't know what melted it, so the entry has to say 'cause unknown'. I've never written that under my name.

If I must write it, I want samples and a date beside it. Kill the Glasswall Elementals at the pit, south of camp, and bring me their fused shards. Ask me about the glass after, and I'll tell you how the entry's going to read.
ab_nothing_is_hot_enough.accept_text: Note the time you take each one. I'll put the hour in the book as well as the date.
ab_nothing_is_hot_enough.turn_in_text:
Here's the entry: cause unknown, sixty feet, south-facing, post-collapse, samples taken, no local heat source identified.

That's it in the book. I feel worse than I expected and better than I deserve.

ab_on_the_box.description:
I was driving the second cart at Nineteen Mile when the road fell in. The lead pair were six lengths ahead of me. The cart went down, I fell off the back, and the ground I landed on held. I didn't do anything clever.

Cartfall Scavengers pick through the wrecks at Cartfall, west of here, every day. There are still people down in those pits. Kill the scavengers and get them off the rim.
ab_on_the_box.accept_text: Keep clear of the edge at Cartfall. It's held so far, but I wouldn't bet you on it.

ab_peg_irons.description:
I shod kodo for nine years. Now I make iron tips for survey pegs. Limestone Crawlers chew those irons off the stakes, and nobody's told me why.

I want to line the next batch with crawler shell and see if they'll leave it alone. Kill the crawlers at the Wide Sink, southwest of camp, and bring me their plates.
ab_peg_irons.accept_text: Bring the plates with the most wear on them. If they chew them anyway, I want to see where.
ab_peg_irons.turn_in_text:
These will do nicely. I tried it with a scrap of shell last month and the crawlers left that peg alone, so now I can line the whole batch.

The survey's stakes are going to be armoured with the animal that eats them. I'd like Peska to write that in her book.

ab_reading_the_pan.description:
I think I can test what I hear, and you won't enjoy it. Limestone Crawlers come up where the ground's thin. If I'm right about the sound, there'll be more of them where the hardpan sounds wrong to me.

I've marked a stretch by the Wide Sink, southwest of camp. Kill the crawlers that come up there and bring me their plates, so I can count them against Peska's rod readings.
ab_reading_the_pan.accept_text: Stamp as you walk. If the ground answers hollow, that's my stretch.
ab_reading_the_pan.turn_in_text:
You got a good handful off a stretch I called thin, and Peska's rod came back at eleven on the stretch either side of it.

I won't call that proof yet. It's the first thing I've had that's even the same shape as proof.

ab_second_peg.description: You turn the broken piece of wood over. It's the top few inches of a survey stake, snapped off clean, as if the ground under it simply dropped away. There's a number burned into the wood, and the burn is still sharp. Somebody took care marking it, which means somebody keeps a list. The surveyor at Fourth Peg, in the north-east corner of the Abyssal Sands, will know which stake it came from.
ab_second_peg.accept_text: You tuck the peg head into your pack. Somebody at Fourth Peg is missing a number.

ab_the_answer_comes_back.description:
I've written her four pages. The first three are sums she can check herself, because she won't trust the rest otherwise.

The fourth page says what's causing it, and she won't like it. Her pits will keep opening until somebody stops what's taking the water. Carry it back to Peska Vane at Fourth Peg, in the northeast corner of the Abyssal Sands. Ask me what's in it first, so you can answer her questions.
ab_the_answer_comes_back.accept_text: Hand it to her and let her read it sitting down.

ab_the_fused_face.description:
There's a pit south of camp called the Glasswall. About sixty feet of its south face has melted into glass. You can see your reflection in it in the afternoon.

Sand needs a furnace's heat to do that. Nothing in this desert burns that hot, and lightning doesn't melt sixty feet in a straight line. Go and look at it for me. Glasswall Elementals wander the rim, so you'll have to kill those to get close.
ab_the_fused_face.accept_text: Go in the afternoon if you can. You'll want to see what the light does on it.

ab_the_lead_pair.description:
I shod kodo for the caravans for years, and some of the ones that went into the pits climbed back out wrong. You'll see Pitfall Kodo around Cartfall, west of camp, still wearing their harness.

They can't be led and they charge the camp's animals, so they have to be put down. Cut the harness off the ones you kill and bring it to me. Every strap has a house mark, and Odd wants the owners told.
ab_the_lead_pair.accept_text: Bring the buckles too if they come away. The marks are stamped on those as well.

ab_the_level_run.description: I need the ground levelled in a straight line west of here, from the peg to Cartfall and on to the First Hole at the far west end. A straight line means walking it, so you can't go round the bad stretches, however much you'd like to. Pit Shrikes nest along that line where the ground's thin, and they'll come at anyone who walks past. I've carried the staff behind three surveyors out here, and I'd like to carry it behind one who gets to the end. Walk the line from Fourth Peg to Cartfall and the First Hole, and kill the shrikes you meet so I can follow you with the staff.
ab_the_level_run.accept_text: Keep to the line even when it goes over the bad ground. A bend in it means I start again.

ab_the_long_collapse.description:
The Long Collapse opened eleven months ago, over a single afternoon, and it took twenty-two tiles of ground and a stretch of the old road with it.

It's the only one any of us watched happen. I want the rim walked, and I want it walked by somebody who isn't me, because I've walked it nine times and I've stopped seeing it.

The Long Collapse is south-west of camp, on past the Wide Sink. Sinkhole lurkers den under the rim. Kill the ones you meet and bring me their spurs, because Peska says the spur tells her how deep they came up from.
ab_the_long_collapse.accept_text: Walk it slowly and look at the far side as much as the near one. That's the side I've stopped seeing.

ab_the_south_facing.description:
Twice a year the sun hits the Glasswall at the right angle and it throws the light back at the camp. For forty minutes we're the brightest place in Tanaris. Tobbit says it's a hazard and Hask says it's beautiful.

I like to stand on the rise and watch it, and lately Glasswall Elementals have been coming up the slope at me from the pit, south of here. Get rid of them for me. Then ask me about the glass, and you'll hear what the rest of the camp thinks.
ab_the_south_facing.accept_text: Bring me a bit of their glass if any comes off. I'd like a piece for the kitchen window.
ab_the_south_facing.turn_in_text:
That's much better. Now I can watch it without keeping one eye on the slope.

It's the only thing out here that keeps a schedule, and I look forward to it.

ab_the_throats.description:
The Throats are the two with no floor, and they're the two I won't go down past forty feet.

There's something living in them that's wet. I need scale off whatever you can reach, and somebody else has to be holding the knife, because I've been down that hole nine times and the tenth is where people stop coming back.

The Throats are in the far south-west, the whole desert away from this camp. The wet things are deepwater horrors. Kill them at the rim and cut the scale off them while it's still wet.
ab_the_throats.accept_text: Bring a sack that doesn't leak. The scale has to reach me wet, or I learn nothing.

ab_the_two_without.description:
Nine have floors and two don't. Underlight is south of here, down the east side. The Throats are in the far south-west.

I've been down both to the end of my line, and the line is a hundred and twenty feet, and it doesn't reach anything.

Walk both rims for me in one day, in order, and tell me whether you come back thinking what I think.

Deepwater horrors climb out of both. Kill what you meet on each rim.
ab_the_two_without.accept_text: Take water for the whole day. There's nowhere to fill up between them.

ab_the_wrong_direction.description:
There's a pit down the east side, south of camp. The camp calls it Underlight, and Peska's grudgingly started calling it that in the book too.

There's light coming up out of that hole. You can't see it at noon, but I fly over it after dark, and you can read by it from the saddle. Light doesn't come up out of the ground. Tolls won't fly over it any more, and she's the bravest bird I've had.

Go and stand on the rim. Everybody has to once. The Deepwater Horrors come up out of it after dark, so kill the ones on the rim before you stand there.
ab_the_wrong_direction.accept_text: Look straight down into it, not across. It's different from above.

ab_three_month_contract.description:
I came out with the second camp on a three-month contract.

That was two years and two camps ago, and nobody has ever mentioned the contract again, including me.

I'm not complaining, and I'd like that understood before I ask you for anything. Go south and make the run to the Throats survivable for a woman carrying glass, and I'll tell you why I stayed.

The saltbone revenants and the sinkhole lurkers are what make that run dangerous. Kill them along it.
ab_three_month_contract.accept_text: I'll have a drink waiting when you're back. It's not the good stuff, but it's cold.

ab_up_through_the_floor.description:
Everybody out here talks about what went into the holes, the carts and the kodo and the road. Nobody wants to talk about what came out, and I'm the one standing at the gate when it does.

Vizzi's been down most of them on a rope, and she says the crawlers and the oozes weren't living on this desert before the change, because this desert couldn't feed them. The holes opened a way, and it goes both directions.

The nearest of them are at Cartfall, west of camp, and along the Glasswall to the south.
ab_up_through_the_floor.accept_text: If you see anything new come out of the ground while you're out there, tell me before you tell Vizzi.

ab_wait_and_read.description:
One reading tells me where the ground is. It takes a second reading at the same stake, a few days later, to tell me if it's moving. I took the first set four days ago.

Take the second set for me at the Wide Sink, southwest of here, and at Cartfall to the west. While you're at the Wide Sink, kill the Hollowing Oozes on the rim. They eat limestone, and I'd like fewer of them eating that one.
ab_wait_and_read.accept_text: Read the stakes at the same hour I did, or near it. The sand moves differently in the heat.

ab_what_the_birds_know.description:
I'm a cook, so here's a free method: open the bird. A Pit Shrike hunts the thin ground and the rim, and it'll eat anything it can carry. What's in its crop is a list of what's living in a place you can't get to.

Hask asked me to find out what they've been eating, because he reckons crops will tell him more about the floor of those holes than Vizzi's rope has in a year. He'd like that on record before he says it to her face.
ab_what_the_birds_know.accept_text: Bring the crops whole and I'll open them here. I'd rather do the sorting myself.

ab_what_the_salt_cured.description:
I'm a brewer, so I know what brine does to bone. The Saltbone Revenants that come up out of the Long Collapse, southwest of camp, have been cured in brine.

The nearest brine I know of is the Shimmering Flats, four days northwest. So either somebody's hauling salt out here, or there's brine under our feet. Kill the revenants and bring me their knucklebones, and I'll test the salt against what I've got from the Flats.
ab_what_the_salt_cured.accept_text: Don't lick your fingers after. I mean it, because people do.

dd_down_the_wide_sink.description:
Vizzi's had my rope down every hole on this map, and mostly it comes back up and tells her nothing.

The Wide Sink's different. Her line goes slack partway, so there's a floor down there, and the rubble has slid into a ramp you could walk down. She'd like somebody to walk it, and since it's my rope, I get to choose who.

The Wide Sink is the big pit south-west of this camp. At the bottom you'll be in what we've been calling the Dry Deep. Keep going until you reach a cavern so big your lamp won't find the far wall. Peska named it the Drained Sea off Vizzi's lamp readings. Then come back and tell us what's really down there.
dd_down_the_wide_sink.accept_text: Take two lamps. The first one always goes out sooner than you'd like.

dd_mother_of_crawlers.description:
The Limestone Crawlers came up through the depot floor again last night. They chewed a cart axle, and that's the third this season. I keep four carts and I need all four to strike this town in a day, which is the only reason the port keeps paying for it.

Peska says the crawlers nest in holes the oozes leave. That's true up here. But Vizzi says there's a shelf under the Throat, deep in the south-west of the Dry Deep, where the floor is nothing but eggs and something big sits in the middle of them.

Go down the Throat, take the passage south-west at the bottom to the Brood Shelf, and kill what's sitting there. The crew call it the Mother of Crawlers.
dd_mother_of_crawlers.accept_text: Watch your feet on the shelf. If it's all eggs like Vizzi says, you'll want to be careful where you stand.

dd_teeth_of_the_old_sea.description:
Hask brought me a tooth from under Nineteen Mile. He found it lying loose on a shelf of rock that's all bones, things that swam, set in the wall where the sea floor stood up on its edge.

I put it to my file and the file lost. I've shod kodo for nine years and nothing has ever beaten that file.

The tooth wasn't old, though. Hask says the thing it came from is still down there on the Fossil Shelf, alive, and the crew call it the Coil of the Old Sea. Go down Nineteen Mile Pit, south-west of town, and at the bottom take the passage that climbs away east. It goes nowhere else. Kill it and bring me its teeth. I'll have a file out of them that doesn't lose.
dd_teeth_of_the_old_sea.accept_text: Pull the teeth with the root still on. The root's where the hardness is.
dd_teeth_of_the_old_sea.turn_in_text:
Every one of them is sharper than my best edge. You couldn't buy these anywhere.

The first file goes on the Fourth Peg forge. This one's for you. I made it the old way, because the new file isn't cut yet.

dd_the_weight_of_the_floor.description:
There's something standing in the Drained Sea. Every lamp I lower near it gets smashed.

From what I could see it's made of the same stone as the roof. I think a piece of the roof came down in one lump and then got up. Peska's crew won't go near it and I can't survey past it.

We've been calling it the Weight of the Floor. Go back down the Wide Sink, south-west of this camp, into the Dry Deep. It's in the middle of the Drained Sea, the biggest cavern down there. Kill it if you can.
dd_the_weight_of_the_floor.accept_text: Don't stand under it when it falls. It came down from the roof once already.

dd_up_a_different_hole.description:
Vizzi says the holes all join up underneath. I want to know if that's true, because I lost a cart and a team down Nineteen Mile and I never found out where they ended up.

Go down into the Dry Deep by any pit with a ramp. See if you can walk to the bottom of Nineteen Mile Pit, the Long Collapse and the Underlight without coming back up. You'll know each one by the daylight coming down the shaft.
dd_up_a_different_hole.accept_text: If you find anything of mine down Nineteen Mile, a harness or a box, bring it up.
dd_up_a_different_hole.turn_in_text:
All three, and you never came up once.

Then I know where my team ended up, and I can get down there myself to see to them. I've wanted to for a long time.

dd_what_eats_the_floor.description:
If it's one cavern under all of this, then I've been asking the wrong question. I've been trying to work out whether the pits have stopped opening. What I should be asking is how long the roof will last.

The Hollowing Oozes dissolve limestone and the Limestone Crawlers nest in the holes the oozes leave. Up here that's a nuisance. Down in the Dry Deep they're eating the pillars that hold the roof up.

Go down and kill as many of both as you can, and have a look at the pillars while you're there.
dd_what_eats_the_floor.accept_text: Knock on the pillars as you pass. If one sounds hollow, mark it for me.

dd_where_the_brine_comes_from.description:
I told Peska the revenants had been cured in brine and that the nearest brine was four days away. I was wrong about the second part.

Vizzi's lamp went down the First Hole last week and came back up crusted white. There's salt under the First Hole, in layers, where the old sea dried out a bit at a time. Vizzi calls it the Salt Galleries. It's past the bottom of the First Hole, to the north-west, as far as the cave goes.

Something down in the salt is curing them. Vizzi saw a revenant twice the size of the others, standing in the salt like it was waiting. The crew call it the Salt Widow. Kill it, and bring me a lump of the salt it stands in.
dd_where_the_brine_comes_from.accept_text: Bring a big lump, not a scraping. I want to brew a test batch with it.
